name: Geoffrey Palmer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Geoffrey Palmer is one of the largest apartment developers in Los Angeles, with more than 13,000 units in the greater L.A. metro area.
Palmer got his start developing residential projects in Los Angeles in the 1970s before starting his own firm, G.H. Palmer Associates, in 1978.
His first projects were condos in the Santa Clarita valley in north Los Angeles county; he built his first apartment complex in Santa Clarita in 1985.
Palmer is a major financial backer of former president Donald Trump, donating nearly $20 million to his campaigns and PACs from 2016 to 2024.
Palmer gained notoriety for his lawsuits against the city of L.A., most famously by successfully suing to block its affordable housing policy in 2009.
forbes_facts: Palmer has spent millions of dollars to defeat rent control ballot initiatives in California in 2018 and 2020, plus a failed attempt to recall Gov. Gavin Newsom.
Palmer is a competitive polo player in France.

name: Bianca Rinehart
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Bianca Rinehart is the eldest daughter of Australian mining magnate Gina Rinehart and is a trustee of the Hope Margaret Hancock Trust.
She replaced her mother as trustee in 2015, after a lengthy court battle.
The trust owns nearly a quarter of Gina Rinehart's Hancock Prospecting, on behalf of her four children.
She has a degree in hospitality and hotel management from Flinders University in Adelaide.
Hancock disclosed that as of September 2023 it had provided A$5.44 billion for dividends that will be paid after the dispute between Bianca and her brother John against their mother is resolved.
forbes_facts: She worked briefly at global miner Rio Tinto. Her job included driving a huge haul truck.
She slept with a hammer under her mattress after her grandfather, Lang Hancock, married his housekeeper, generating huge publicity.

name: Igor Khudokormov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Igor Khudokormov, a former military officer, is the founder of Prodimex Group, the largest sugar producer in Russia with 14 refineries.
In the 1990s he and his partners, also former military officers, started a sugar import business before snapping up several sugar plants during Russia's privatization.
His Prodimex Group also owns 900,000 hectares of agricultural land.

name: Eustasio Lopez Gonzalez
forbes_bio: Eustasio López González is the owner of Invertur Helsan, a closely held Spanish hotel group.
He co-founded investment company, Hijos de Francisco López Sánchez in 1972, which was the seed of the family's Lopesan Group.

Originally focused on construction and real-estate, Lopez Gonzales pivoted the business into tourism in the 1990s, creating the hotel division that developed Meloneras in south Gran Canaria, including the flagship Lopesan Costa Meloneras, which opened in 2000.
He acquired a majority stake in Germany's IFA Hotels & Touristik in 1999, which became a platform for growth in Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
He remains chairman of the Lopesan Group and continues to oversee its international portfolio, including the 5-star Lopesan Costa Bávaro in Punta Cana.

name: Eduardo Voigt Schwartz
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Eduardo Voigt Schwartz is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, the largest manufacturer of electrical motors in Latin America.
The company was cofounded by his grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt along with former billionaires Eggon Joao da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus (deceased).
A publicly-traded multinational with factories in over ten countries, WEG has annual revenue of approximately $7 billion.
Eduardo does not hold a board seat or any executive position at WEG; and performs and tours as a DJ.

name: Alexander Sixt
forbes_bio: Alexander Sixt, together with his brother, Konstantin, owns 56% of Sixt SE, one of the world's largest car rental companies. They are the co-CEOs.
Their grandfather Martin Sixt founded the firm in 1912. Their father, Erich, took over in 1969 when it was a local operation with just 200 vehicles.
Together with his wife, Regine, Erich turned the company into a global player. He stepped down as CEO in 2021; he is chair of the supervisory board.
Sixt SE, which went public in 1986, had 2021 revenues of around $2.5 billion, 7,000 employees and some 2,000 locations in over 100 countries.
Alexander joined Sixt in 2009; he and his brother Konstantin were appointed co-CEOs in 2021 after their father stepped down.
forbes_facts: In 2015, Alexander and his brother Konstantin joined Sixt's executive board.
His mom is still active in the company, in her role as Senior Executive Vice President of Marketing.

name: Dong Fan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Dong Fan chairs Jafron Biomedical, which went public in August 2016 on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.
Dong, who holds a 48% stake in Jafron, is a graduate of Shanghai University of Finance and Sun Yet-Sen University in China.
Jafron was founded in 1989.

name: Peng Yonghe
appears_on: Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun China (2023-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)

name: Kathy Fields
forbes_bio: Dermatologist Kathy Fields and her business partner Katie Rodan have created two successful skincare brands: Proactiv Solutions and Rodan + Fields.
In May 2018, private equity firm TPG spent $1 billion to buy a 25% stake in Rodan + Fields.
Rodan + Fields borrowed $600 million in junk bonds in June 2018 and used it to pay the founders a dividend.
Rodan + Fields did not reveal 2018 revenue, but it hit $1.5 billion in 2017; the direct marketing firm conducts sales through 300,000 'consultants.'
In 2016, the two dermatologists sold their Proactiv royalties to a joint venture between Guthy Renker and Nestle, which markets the product.
forbes_facts: Fields and Rodan met as dermatology residents at Stanford University.
Fields is also an assistant dermatology professor at the University of California, San Francisco, and has a private practice in San Francisco.

name: Zhao Ding
forbes_bio: Zhao Ding is the deputy chairman and deputy general manager of Chinese snacks retailer Busy Ming Group.
The company went public in Hong Kong in January 2026, raising $470 million.
It sells under the Busy for You and Super Ming brands, offering products such as small-packaged biscuits and nuts across a network of about 20,000 stores in China.
The group was formed in 2023, when Zhao's Super Ming merged with fellow snacks retailer Busy for You.
Busy for You's founder, Yan Zhou, is also a billionaire.

name: Lev Kvetnoi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Lev Kvetnoi has invested in airports, airport services, banking and cement.
Kvetnoi was the largest shareholder in Moscow's Vnukovo Airport, owning 30% of the project, until he sold out in 2013 and quit its board.
In 2011 he expanded his cement holdings by acquiring one of billionaire Elena Baturina's factories in southern Russia.
forbes_facts: For a time Kvetnoi served as chief executive of a company in billionaire Alisher Usmanov's metals group, but he sold out his interests to Usmanov in 2006.
In the early 1990s, Kvetnoi traded computers with an army friend Andrei Skoch, who is now also billionaire.

name: James Jannard
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Jim Jannard founded sunglasses brand Oakley out of his car in 1975.
He took Oakley public in 1995 and sold it to Luxottica in 2007 for $2.1 billion in cash.
By then he was working on his next project, Red Digital, building high-resolution cameras used in movies like "Avatar" and "The Hobbit." He agreed to sell the business to Nikon in March 2024.
He launched Red Hydrogen One, a holographic smartphone that was plagued with issues, in 2018 but shut down the project in 2019.
forbes_facts: The USC pharmacy student dropped out in the 1960s after clashing with professors over bringing his dog to class.
Jannard named Oakley after his beloved English Setter, Oakley Anne. He has funded a breeder in Washington for decades.

name: Maria Consuelo Dias Branco
forbes_bio: Maria Consuelo Saraiva Leao Dias Branco is the chairperson of the board of directors of M. Dias Branco, a Brazilian food product manufacturer and distributor.
She took over after the death of her husband Francisco Ivens de Sa Dias Branco in 2016, whose father started M. Dias Branco as a small bakery in 1936.
The food production conglomerate specializes in wheat products such as biscuits, pasta, and cake mix; they have acquired over twenty different brands in Latin America.
Maria is the largest individual stakeholder in M. Dias Branco, owning about a third of the public company's shares.
